assistance: AI-assisted (Claude): the TypeScript generator generators/grand-central-terminal.ts was written from the open evidence in the modelling notes (OSM, public lidar and aerials, licensed photographs, published dimensions), reviewed by a human against reference photos, and exported deterministically. No photographic textures.
modelingNotes: Grand Central Terminal — procedural, CC0-1.0, no textures. bun generators/grand-central-terminal.ts

Map frame: x across the building (Vanderbilt -x, Lexington side +x), y along Park Avenue (42nd Street -y), z up, metres. Placed at bearing 29°, the Manhattan grid. Anchor is the centre of the OSM outline's rotated bounding box (way/265947358, 120.6 × 103 m, height 45.8 m), so the model can be exactly symmetrical about x = 0.

Masses: the Beaux-Arts head house (42nd Street front and the two side fronts) under a green copper hip roof; the main concourse rising behind it with its own copper roof and pale skylight ridge; the lower north office block up to the MetLife Building, which is a separate building and is not modelled here.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "grand-central-terminal", model "grand-central-terminal"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/grand-central-terminal.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
To fit six materials, folded grand-central-terminal-granite into grand-central-terminal-flat-roof (ΔE 8.4).
